title: Pressing another Note's × ends Editing
lede: The × cancels its own `pointerdown`, so it is not a **Press**: it never Raises or drags. But that also meant the press never reached `ui.pressed`, so while Note A was in **Editing**, clicking the × on Note B deleted B and left A in Editing, with its **Draft text** unsaved. The glossary says pressing anywhere else ends Editing. Now the × reports the press itself. One line of runtime code; the rest is a test and wording.

steps.title: focus moves to B's ×
steps.explain: Unchanged, and the reason only the mouse path was broken. Focus leaving A's textarea and arriving on B's × bubbles to B's article as a React `focus` event. `focusNote` reports `pressed(b)`, which ends Editing on A. No `pointerdown` happens, so the new line doesn't run.

notes.title: Why report the press, and not end Editing on every delete
notes.detail: Changing `deleted` to end Editing whatever Note is deleted would also fix this, but it changes the documented rule ("ends only if it was that Note") and would end Editing for deletes that no press caused. Reporting the press keeps the glossary's rule as the single reason. The counter-argument: `pressed(id)` is now called in four places in `Note.tsx`.

notes.title: Right or middle button on the ×
notes.detail: `pointerdown` fires for every button, so a right-click on another Note's × now ends Editing without deleting anything (no `click` follows). That matches the article's own `press`, which also reports every button. Read in the code, not run.

notes.title: Where focus goes
notes.detail: `preventDefault` keeps focus in A's textarea, which unmounts when Editing ends, so focus falls to `<body>`. A press on empty Board ends the same way today. Not changed here.
